angle_hi: अशोष्य: हवा से न सूखने योग्य

en.intro: Krishna continues by listing exactly what physical force cannot do to the true self. Listen for the word that describes the limits of water.
en.notice: Krishna uses the word ashosyah, undryable, to show that the inner being cannot be dried by any force. It is eternal, all-pervading, unmoving, and fixed, standing beyond the reach of any physical element.
en.next: The next verse says this self is unseen and beyond thought, so Arjuna should stop grieving.
en.meaning: This embodied self cannot be cut, burned, wetted, or dried. It is eternal, all-pervading, unmoving, fixed, and timeless.

hi.intro: कृष्ण आगे बताते हैं कि भौतिक बल इस आत्मा को क्या नहीं कर सकता। उस शब्द को सुनिए जो पानी की सीमा बताता है।
hi.meaning: यह शरीरी काटा नहीं जा सकता, जलाया नहीं जा सकता, गीला नहीं किया जा सकता और सुखाया भी नहीं जा सकता। यह नित्य है, सब में व्याप्त है, स्थिर है, अचल है और सनातन है।
hi.notice: कृष्ण यहाँ अशोष्य शब्द का प्रयोग करते हैं, जिसका अर्थ है जिसे सुखाया न जा सके। यह शब्द बताता है कि आत्मा पर किसी भी भौतिक तत्व का प्रभाव नहीं पड़ता। यह नित्य, सर्वव्यापी, अचल और सनातन है।

issues: borrowed: "He has already said water cannot wet it, and now he adds that not even the wind can dry it, showing that no natural element can touch the inner self." (This presents the content of the PREVIOUS verse (verse 23, where wind is mentioned) within the NOTICE of verse 24, as if it were part of the current verse's explanation.)

borrowed: "पहले वे कह चुके हैं कि पानी इसे गीला नहीं कर सकता" (This presents the content of the PREVIOUS verse (verse 23) within the NOTICE of verse 24, as if it were part of the current verse's explanation.)

wrong_fact: "अगले श्लोक में कहा गया है कि यह आत्मा अदृश्य है और विचारों से परे है, इसलिए इसे जानकर तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।" (This misrepresents the next verse (2.25). The next verse states 'It is unseen, beyond thought, and said to be unchanged. Therefore, knowing it this way, you should not grieve.' The Hindi notice incorrectly translates 'unchanged' (अपरिमित/अविकार) as 'it is unseen' (यह आत्मा अदृश्य है), borrowing the description of being unseen from the next verse and presenting it as the subject of the current next verse. It also omits 'unchanged' (अविकार) entirely.)

unsupported: "उस शब्द को सुनिए जो पानी की सीमा बताता है" (The instruction asks the user to listen for the word describing the limit of water, but the verse's Sanskrit and Hindi meanings focus on the self being 'undryable' (अशोष्यः/अशोष्य), not water itself. There is no word in this verse that describes the limit of water; rather, water is mentioned as a force that cannot affect the self.)
